meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vitya, wait here for a minute.
See you very soon, daughter!
Before the wedding you must not see me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'видание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'goodbye' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Goodbye, although wait a minute.
Goodbye!
I have a date today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Although I am calm about you.
I wanted to talk with you.
Do you remember anything at all right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vitya, wait here for a minute.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am allowed, I am not the groom.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will start our life over.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Heavy work is forbidden for you right now.

examples.text: Парни, сейчас всё в ваших руках.
examples.trans: Guys, everything is in your hands right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жениться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will get married'.

related.gloss: to we will get married (base verb)
not to we will get married (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и пожениться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will get married on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют пожениться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to we will get married.
